    E. $r = k [A]^{-1}$ (Negative order)
    F. $r = k$ (Zero order)

    H. $r = k [A]^3$ (Third order in A)
    I. $r = k / [A]$ (Inverse first order)
    J. $r = k \ln[A]$ (Complex dependence)

### Method 1: Using Standard Reduction Potentials

The standard cell potential ($E^\circ_{\text{cell}}$) for an electrochemical reaction is calculated using the standard reduction potentials ($E^\circ$) of the half-reactions:
$$E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = E^\circ_{\text{cathode}} - E^\circ_{\text{anode}}$$

1.  **Identify the Half-Reactions:**

        The standard reduction potential for this half-reaction is $E^\circ(\text{O}_2/\text{H}_2\text{O}) = +1.23 \text{ V}$.
    *   **Oxidation (Anode):** Hydrogen oxidation.
        $$2\text{H}_2(g) \rightarrow 4\text{H}^+(aq) + 4e^-$$
        The standard reduction potential for $\text{H}^+/\text{H}_2$ is $E^\circ(\text{H}_2/\text{H}^+) = 0.00 \text{ V}$ (Standard Hydrogen Electrode, SHE).

2.  **Calculate $E^\circ_{\text{cell}}$:**
    $$E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = E^\circ(\text{O}_2/\text{H}_2\text{O}) - E^\circ(\text{H}_2/\text{H}^+)$$
    $$E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = 1.23 \text{ V} - 0.00 \text{ V}$$
    $$E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = 1.23 \text{ V}$$

We can also calculate $E^\circ$ using the relationship:

    $$\Delta G^\circ_{\text{rxn}} = [2 \cdot \Delta G^\circ_f(\text{H}_2\text{O}(l))] - [2 \cdot \Delta G^\circ_f(\text{H}_2(g))]$$
    $$\Delta G^\circ_{\text{rxn}} = 2 \cdot (-56,690 \text{ cal/mol}) = -113,380 \text{ cal/mol}$$
